Results in an invented model; real-world testing is still needed

An earlier Worldwright project used an invented computer model to compare responses to a shared problem. In its reported tests, the overall ranking changed when the model’s urgency changed.

Open each part of the result. Every tested case still involved tradeoffs. The model has not been shown to predict real communities, so its rankings do not tell us what people should do.

Open each part of the computer result. Keep its limits beside its ranking.

Words used here
synthetic model
An invented model for exploring assumptions. Its outcomes are not observations of real people or communities.
Pareto tradeoff
A choice where improving one quantity comes with a loss in another. A single overall score can hide that loss.
Read the fuller explanation

The older Worldwright research programme studies authored synthetic interventions. Its landscape reports a conditional finding: with delivery failures disabled, the lower-urgency cells favor mediation in an aggregate diagnostic, while the higher-urgency cells favor immediate visible action.

The same source retains Pareto tradeoffs in every cell. A winning aggregate does not mean every coordinate improves. The mechanisms and their real-world calibration remain unidentified, so these results do not authorize humanitarian policy or explain a person’s circumstances.

Choose which part of the reported model result to inspect. The encounter changes the reading of an existing synthetic record; it does not rerun the model or tell you what a real community should do.

The reported ranking changes with urgency and with the chosen score. The model has not been shown to predict real communities or decide what is morally right.

Worldwright research: current landscape

The older research model is distinct from this storytelling product. Its frozen cells expose urgency-dependent aggregate rankings and Pareto tradeoffs under declared assumptions. Its mechanisms remain empirically unidentified; no policy, personal advice or moral authority follows from the rankings.
